Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Church life · Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

believe in verb

also believe in God

late Latin

Vulg. Jo. 6.35: quī crēdit in mē
Aug. Serm. 144.2 (Lewis & Short, s.v. crēdō)

crēdere in (+ accusative)

phrase: crēdō with in and the accusative

believe in (God, Christ)

The construction of Christian Latin, and of the Creed, Crēdō in ūnum Deum. Augustine marks the difference: believing that Christ exists is Chrīstum esse crēdere, believing in him is in Chrīstum crēdere.

Other words

  • deōs putāre — believe in the gods

    phrase · also used · classical · Cic. Div. 1.104: id ipsum est deōs nōn putāre (Lewis & Short, s.v. putō)

    The classical way, of the pagan gods: to hold that they exist and to heed their signs.

Examples

  • Crēdō, Domine; adjuvā incrēdulitātem meam.

    I believe, Lord; help my unbelief.Vulg. Mc. 9.23 (the Stuttgart text omits Domine)

  • et quī crēdit in mē, nōn sitiet umquam

    and whoever believes in me will never thirstVulg. Jo. 6.35

  • Chrīstum esse crēdit, nōn in Chrīstum crēdit

    (whoever has faith without hope and love) believes that Christ is, not in ChristAug. Serm. 144.2 (Lewis & Short)

See also believe, church.

SourcesLewis & Short: credo · Lewis & Short: puto

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
